entries.sentence: Type 1 diabetes is a lifelong condition in which the pancreas produces little or no insulin.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: It is an autoimmune condition: the immune system damages the insulin-producing cells of the pancreas.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Without insulin the body cannot move glucose out of the blood and into cells, so regular insulin treatment is needed to keep glucose levels in a healthy range.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS notes that the tendency can run in families.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Researchers have not pinned down what sets off the autoimmune process, and research reviews have suggested that viral infections and other factors may play a part.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Type 1 is a different condition from type 2 diabetes, which accounts for the large majority of diabetes worldwide.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS lists the classic early signs as needing the toilet more, being thirsty, feeling tired and losing weight, often remembered as the four Ts.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: NIDDK notes that some people first find out they have type 1 diabetes when they develop signs of diabetic ketoacidosis.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A GP will usually test a urine sample and may check blood glucose, then send the person to hospital for assessment.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS says people usually stay in hospital until the blood test results are back, which is generally the same day.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS says symptoms of type 1 diabetes can appear over a few days or weeks.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The other signs it lists are blurred vision, sweet or fruity-smelling breath, slow-healing cuts and frequent infections.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Because diabetic ketoacidosis can be the first sign, the NHS advises calling 999 or going to A&E if symptoms worsen quickly, or if stomach pain, sleepiness or confusion, or fast, deep breathing develop.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A same-day GP appointment is the usual route for the earlier warning signs in a child or young person.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS says treatment means taking insulin for life and regularly checking blood glucose.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Most people take both a long-acting insulin, once or twice a day, and a rapid-acting insulin before meals.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: This pattern is known as basal-bolus treatment.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Insulin can be given with pens or by a pump, a device worn on the body that delivers small amounts of insulin through the day and night.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Pump therapy can be used by adults, teenagers and children with adult supervision.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The amount of mealtime insulin varies with the blood glucose level before the meal and with the amount of carbohydrate eaten, which is why carbohydrate counting is taught.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: NHS inform lists the other ongoing tasks: checking glucose, recognising the signs of a hypo, attending check-ups and planning for driving and pregnancy.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: One NHS 111 Wales page stresses that treatment should not be stopped during illness, and that the treatment plan may say whether a temporary increase is needed.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: A hypo is a lower-than-normal level of glucose in the blood.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: NICE lists dizziness, tiredness, hunger, shaking and sweating among the symptoms, and notes that some people with long-standing diabetes do not always spot the warning signs.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: NHS inform says a hypo happens when injected insulin moves too much glucose out of the bloodstream.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Common triggers include too much insulin, a skipped meal, vigorous exercise and drinking alcohol on an empty stomach.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Mild hypos are usually treated with something sugary.

entries.sentence: Severe ones may need an injection of glucagon into a muscle or glucose given into a vein.

entries.sentence: NICE says the annual review should check that the person can recognise the symptoms of a hypo.

entries.sentence: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) occurs when a lack of insulin lets harmful substances called ketones build up in the blood.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: It can be life-threatening and needs urgent treatment in hospital.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: Diabetes UK lists thirst, passing urine more, stomach pain, sickness, deep breathing, fruity-smelling breath, tiredness or confusion and blurred vision.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: It says symptoms usually develop over about 24 hours but can be faster.

entries.sentence: The NHS advises calling 999 or going to A&E if the symptoms are getting worse quickly, or if there is stomach pain, sleepiness or confusion, or fast, deep breathing.

entries.sentence: People with type 1 diabetes are taught to test for ketones when they are unwell, and the NHS gives the blood and urine levels at which to ring 999, or at which to contact the diabetes team for advice.

entries.sentence: Untreated, DKA can cause vomiting, dehydration, unconsciousness and death.

entries.sentence: Over time, high glucose can damage blood vessels and nerves.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: The NHS describes three main areas.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: In the eyes, damage to blood vessels can cause sight problems (diabetic retinopathy) and, uncommonly, blindness, so adults and children aged 12 or over are offered eye screening every year.
entries.note: first pass: written from the retrieved search summary text; attributed to the page(s) whose title matches (summaries blend pages)

entries.sentence: In the feet, nerve damage means small cuts may go unnoticed and can become ulcers, so the NHS advises checking the feet every day and having a foot examination at least once a year.

entries.sentence: In the kidneys, damage usually causes no symptoms at first, so a test is advised every year.

entries.sentence: NICE describes an annual review that covers foot checks, dental checks for gum disease and screening for kidney and nerve problems.

entries.sentence: Cholesterol and blood pressure are also checked, and blood pressure is checked in children too.
